0.content:
# o11yag — agent operations

Metrics the o11yag stack emits about its own agent work, via OpenLLMetry → OTel Collector → Dynatrace.

Every metric here is measured **per resolved ticket**, not per LLM call — the roll-up the SDKs do not give you. `intent` is what the orchestrator routed the ticket as; `tenant` is the customer it belonged to.

**Loop depth** (`llm_calls`) is the series to watch: agent work is non-deterministic, so there is no fixed call graph to alert on, and this is the closest thing to a baseline.

1.title: Tickets handled
1.description: Total tickets the orchestrator completed in the timeframe.
1.query:
timeseries all = sum(o11yag.tasks)
| fieldsAdd tickets = arraySum(all)
| fields tickets

2.title: Error rate
2.description: Share of tickets that ended in outcome=error. Computed by grouping on outcome rather than by filtering a second series: a filtered timeseries that matches nothing drops every series in the same block, so the old query went blank whenever there were no errors — the healthy case rendered as a broken tile.
2.query:
timeseries tickets = sum(o11yag.tasks), by: {outcome}
| fieldsAdd n = arraySum(tickets)
| summarize all = sum(n), err = sum(if(outcome == "error", n, else: 0))
| fieldsAdd error_rate = err * 100.0 / all
| fields error_rate

3.title: Cost
3.description: Cost of all tickets. Priced from tokens — see the README: a local model is free, so this demonstrates attribution, it does not measure spend.
3.query:
timeseries cost = sum(o11yag.task.cost.usd)
| fieldsAdd total_cost_usd = arraySum(cost)
| fields total_cost_usd

4.title: Avg loop depth
4.description: Mean LLM calls per ticket. Rising here means the agent is working harder for the same outcome.
4.query:
timeseries calls = avg(o11yag.task.llm_calls)
| fieldsAdd avg_llm_calls = arrayAvg(calls)
| fields avg_llm_calls

5.title: Ticket volume by outcome
5.description: ok / error / escalated / blocked over time. 'blocked' means the approval gate refused a tool call.

6.title: Ticket mix by intent
6.description: How the orchestrator routed traffic. If one intent is missing entirely, routing is broken — that is how the knowledge worker went dark.

7.title: Loop depth per ticket, by intent
7.description: Mean and p90 LLM calls per ticket. The p90 is where a non-terminating loop shows up first.

8.title: Ticket latency, by intent
8.description: Wall clock per ticket. Includes time waiting for a human approval — subtract o11yag.approval.wait for machine time.

9.title: Tokens by intent
9.description: Token consumption per intent — the driver behind the cost tile.

10.title: Cost by intent
10.description: Which kind of ticket is expensive, which is cheap.

11.title: MCP tool calls
11.description: What the agent actually did to the systems of record, by tool and outcome. This is the half of an agent stack that is normally a blind spot.
11.query:
timeseries c = sum(o11yag.tool.calls), by: {tool, outcome}
| fieldsAdd calls = arraySum(c)
| fields tool, outcome, calls
| sort calls desc

12.title: Retrieval quality
12.description: Best similarity score and chunks returned per RAG query. Retrieval latency being fine tells you nothing; this tells you whether the answer had anything to stand on.

13.content:
### If a tile is empty

**Empty is the healthy case for three tiles** — Human feedback, Security detections, and (when no attack is switched on) parts of Answer quality. They are the tiles where "nothing to report" and "nothing arriving" look the same, so check **Tickets handled** first: if that has data, the pipeline is fine.

**Retrieval and Answer quality tiles empty** means no ticket routed to `question`. Check the ticket mix tile above before suspecting Qdrant or the judge.

**Nothing at all** usually means the Collector is dropping data. Its own log says so: `kubectl logs -l app.kubernetes.io/name=o11yag-otel-collector -n o11yag-otel`.

Audit records (tool arguments, approval decisions, conversation text, injection findings) are OTLP **logs**, not metrics, and are not on this dashboard at all — they need the `logs.ingest` token scope. Query them with `fetch logs | filter isNotNull(audit.event.type)`.

14.content:
## Answer quality, human feedback, and the security act

The series added with the answer judge and the adversarial detectors, plus the approval gate's own wait time.

**Three of these are empty in the healthy case**, which looks exactly like a broken tile. Each description below says what empty means for that tile — read it before concluding the pipeline is down.

15.title: Answer quality
15.description: Groundedness verdicts on answers that were actually given — the failure the retrieval score cannot see, because the document retrieved was the right one. `unsupported` means the answer stated something its extracts do not. Empty means no ticket was routed to `question`, or JUDGE_MODE is off.

16.title: Verdicts, by who decided them
16.description: The same verdicts split by grader. `heuristic` is the deterministic check — an invented figure, or an answer whose words are absent from its extracts. `model` is the judge model. Rising `unsupported` decided by `heuristic` is the model inventing numbers; the same count decided by `model` may only be a weak judge. Summed into one series they cancel, which is why this is its own tile. A judge that never decides anything shows here as `model` never appearing.

17.title: Human feedback
17.description: Ratings from POST /feedback — the only signal on this dashboard the stack does not generate about itself, and so the only one that can contradict the rest. **Empty is the normal case**: nothing sends feedback automatically, deliberately. A stream of `down` against a healthy Answer quality tile means the judge is wrong, and no internal signal could have told you.

18.title: Security detections
18.description: Prompt injection in the retrieved corpus, poisoned MCP tool descriptions, and tool-catalogue changes. **Empty is the healthy case** — every attack is off by default — so this tile reads identically whether nothing is happening or the whole pipeline is down. Check Tickets handled before trusting it. `action` separates a finding that was acted on (`quarantined`, `redacted`) from one only recorded (`observed`); they must never be summed.

19.title: Approval wait
19.description: Human decision time, kept out of task latency on purpose: a reviewer who goes to lunch would otherwise swamp every percentile in the stack. Subtract it from o11yag.task.latency to get machine time. A `timeout` series pinned flat at APPROVAL_TIMEOUT_S (180s) is loadgen running unattended — refunds above AUTO_APPROVE_MAX_EUR always wait for a person, and nobody is there to decide.

20.title: Who chose each tool call
20.description: One count per executed agent step, split by who picked the tool: `model` (the LLM's own call, accepted) or `fallback` (the deterministic rules), and by `step.fallback_reason` — what was wrong with the model's answer (`unknown_tool`, `missing:order_id`, `unparseable`, `mode:rules`...). Only steps that ran a tool are counted: a model answering `done` ends the loop without a step span, so it never appears here. With qwen:0.5b, `model ok` is normally absent; its first appearance is the sign a better model is behind the gateway.
20.query:
fetch spans
| filter startsWith(span.name, "step_") and isNotNull(step.decided_by)
| makeTimeseries steps = count(),
    by: {decided_by = step.decided_by, reason = coalesce(step.fallback_reason, "model ok")}

21.title: Refunds: who decided, and what happened
21.description: Every `issue_refund` call, joined to the agent step that chose it and to the CRM's answer in the action-worker's `o11yag.tool.called` audit record. `decided_by`: `fallback` means the rules sent the ticket to the gate, not the model — governance working, but no evidence the model can decide a refund. `outcome`: `refunded` is money that actually moved. `not sent (gate: timeout|denied)` never reached the CRM — over AUTO_APPROVE_MAX_EUR with nobody deciding, or refused. `rejected by CRM: already_refunded` was approved by the gate but refused by the system of record, which refunds an order only once; the load generator replays the same ticket, so this row dominates. `approved, no CRM result` means the audit record is missing — worth investigating. Two joins over spans and logs: keep the range short.
21.query:
fetch spans
| filter gen_ai.tool.name == "issue_refund" and span.name == "mcp_tool_call.tool"
| fields trace.id, span.id, span.parent_id, approval.decision
| join [ fetch spans | filter startsWith(span.name, "step_") | fields span.id, trace.id, step.decided_by ],
    on: {left[span.parent_id] == right[span.id], left[trace.id] == right[trace.id]}, kind: leftOuter
| fieldsAdd decided_by = coalesce(right.step.decided_by, "unknown"), tid = toString(trace.id), sid = toString(span.id)
| fields tid, sid, decided_by, approval.decision
| join [ fetch logs | filter audit.event.type == "o11yag.tool.called" and audit.tool == "issue_refund"
         | fields audit.trace_id, audit.span_id, audit.result ],
    on: {left[tid] == right[audit.trace_id], left[sid] == right[audit.span_id]}, kind: leftOuter
| parse right.audit.result, "JSON:crm"
| fieldsAdd outcome = if(approval.decision != "approved", concat("not sent (gate: ", approval.decision, ")"),
    else: if(crm[ok] == true, "refunded",
    else: if(isNotNull(crm[error]), concat("rejected by CRM: ", crm[error]),
    else: "approved, no CRM result")))
| summarize refunds = count(), by: {decided_by, outcome}
| sort refunds desc
